(AP PHOTO) Credit: AAP Hungary's PM to scrap Orban-era ban on gay adoption Staff Writers Reuters 13 September 2026, 3:17am Copy link Share story Hungary's government will change legislation passed in 2020 by Viktor Orban's former regime that had effectively banned adoption by gay and lesbian couples, Prime Minister Peter Magyar says. Adoption in Hungary, a European Union member state, by gay and lesbian couples was possible until late 2020 if one partner applied as a single person. Under the law passed by Orban's right-wing Fidesz party in 2020, single people had to have their adoption requests approved by the family affairs minister, which has amounted to an effective ban. Magyar ousted Orban after 16 years in a landslide election win in April. Changing the system of adoption would be a significant measure to restore LGBTQ rights. "We can state unequivocally that we will change this system: it should not be the minister, a politician ... who makes the decision in such cases, but rather professionals capable of determining the conditions under which a given young child can achieve ... a life that allows them to become a happy and harmonious member of society," Magyar said. Orban, who cast himself as a defender of what he called Christian values from Western liberalism, passed laws ending the change of gender in personal documents, effectively halting adoption by same-sex couples and banning materials in schools seen as promoting homosexuality or gender transition. The erosion of LGBTQI rights had a traumatic effect on the community. Orban's government violated European law with rules prohibiting or restricting access to LGBTQI content, which stigmatise and marginalise gay and trans people, the European Court of Justice ruled in April, just before the election. Hungary has never allowed gay marriage but still recognises civil unions. https://www.dw.com/en/south-korea-demand.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NcGH South Korea is angry that Ukraine disclosed the POW transfer, which was meant to stay secret Image: Daniel Gnap/NurPhoto/picture alliance Advertisement South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Friday threatened Ukraine with "further measures" if Kyiv does not issue a public apology for revealing that North Korean POWs were sent to South Korea . Seoul has reacted sharply to Ukraine's disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean soldiers captured while fighting for Russia, warning that Pyongyang could target their families. What has led to the rift between Seoul and Kyiv? Last week, Lee expressed his regret hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had disclosed the transfer of the soldiers while speaking at the United Nations. Since then, South Korea and Ukraine have been at loggerheads, with Seoul demanding an apology from Kyiv . "If the refusal to acknowledge the facts and issue a public apology continues, we will take additional ​measures," Lee said in a post on X. Lee also accused Kyiv of making him out to be a "liar." Prisoner swap: From North to South Korea via Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video South Korea claims that Kyiv violated an agreement to keep the transfer of the two soldiers to Seoul confidential to protect them. However, Ukrainian officials have denied that such an agreement existed. Ukrainian media on Thursday cited Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha as saying that Kyiv is trying to mend ties with Seoul. "I would not like to call this an incident. Let's say, it's a diplomatic misunderstanding," Sybiha told ⁠journalists ​at an event, according to Ukrainian news agency RBC-Ukraine. "South Korea is an important country for us. And I very much hope for momentum, continued cooperation, and concrete results that we are indeed achieving with them," he said.
